requirements.title: Intrinsic and extension operation categories have the Table 10.1 precedence order
requirements.definition: For expressions formed under 10.1.2, intrinsic and extension operations are interpreted according to the relative precedence categories in Table 10.1 unless parentheses change the order in which operands are combined. The order is: defined unary, exponentiation, multiplication/division, unary plus/minus, binary plus/minus, character concatenation, relational, logical NOT, logical AND, logical OR, logical EQV/NEQV, and defined binary.

pending.power-before-unary-minus: PENDING positive-control source shape assigning -2**2 to an integer result and comparing with literal -4, with parenthesized repair (-2)**2 giving literal 4. The independent oracle is integer exponentiation and negation over small literals; no operand side effect or evaluation order is observed.
pending.multiply-before-binary-plus: PENDING positive-control source shape 2+3*4 with literal oracle 14 and parenthesized contrast (2+3)*4 with literal 20. Integer literals make the precedence observation non-vacuous and avoid floating-point rewrite latitude.
pending.unary-before-binary-plus: PENDING positive-control source shape -3 + 10 with literal oracle 7, where unary minus is the leading add-op on the first add-operand and binary plus combines with the second operand. A companion (-(3+10)) may provide a parenthesized contrast under 10.1.2 ownership; no source with consecutive numeric operators such as A + -B is used.
pending.character-before-relational: PENDING positive-control source shape ('AB'//'CD' == 'ABCD') in a logical context with literal true oracle. Character concatenation and relational result semantics remain 10.1.5.3 and 10.1.5.5 dependencies.
pending.relational-before-logical-or: PENDING positive-control source shape .false. .or. 2+3 >= 5 with a true-branch literal oracle. The numeric and relational subresults are independently small integer facts; the plan observes the parsed interpretation, not evaluation order.
pending.not-before-and: PENDING positive-control source shape .not. .false. .and. .false. with literal false oracle and parenthesized contrast .not.(.false..and..false.) yielding true. No short-circuit or side effect is part of the oracle.
pending.and-before-or: PENDING positive-control source shape .true. .or. .false. .and. .false. with literal true oracle and parenthesized contrast (.true..or..false.).and..false. yielding false. All operands are literals to avoid evaluation-order claims.
pending.or-before-eqv: PENDING positive-control source shape .true. .or. .false. .eqv. .false. with a literal false oracle and parenthesized contrast .true..or.(.false..eqv..false.) yielding true. Logical interpretation remains 10.1.5.4 dependent.
pending.defined-binary-lowest: PENDING positive-control source shape 1+2 .join. 3*4 using a valid defined binary operator whose function returns a decimal encoding of its two integer arguments. The literal oracle distinguishes intrinsic operations as operands before the defined binary call; operation definition remains 10.1.6 and 15.4.3.4.2 owned.
pending.parentheses-override-category-precedence: PENDING positive-control source shape (2+3)*4 and 2+(3*4) in the same program with independent literal oracles 20 and 14. The contrast proves parentheses changed operand combination without relying on processor evaluation sequence.

requirements.oracle: Use integer, character, and logical literals or non-associative defined operations to make precedence observable. Do not infer grouping from an associative intrinsic operation whose value would be unchanged.
requirements.oracle_limitation: This source-only catalogue records pending plans only. It creates no Fortran test program, invokes no processor, approves no fixture or oracle, and claims no coverage. Future fixtures must use independently derived literal or inquiry oracles and must not infer evaluation order, short-circuiting, which operand was evaluated, or whether an operand was evaluated. They must not rely on compiler agreement, address arithmetic, TRANSFER, emitted assembly, undefined reads, or a floating-point result that 10.1.7 or 10.1.8 permits to differ through omitted evaluation or mathematically equivalent rewriting.

requirements.title: A defined operation has the precedence of its operator
requirements.definition: When an operation is a defined operation, its precedence is not determined by the defining procedure but by the operator token used for the operation. A defined operation that extends an intrinsic operator uses that intrinsic operator's Table 10.1 precedence, while dotted defined unary and defined binary operators use their extension rows.

pending.extended-intrinsic-operator-precedence: PENDING positive-control source shape extending intrinsic operator ** for a derived type with a non-associative function result, then combining it with a lower-precedence intrinsic or defined operation. The literal oracle is the function's encoded result; generic validity and defined-operation interpretation remain 10.1.6/15.4.3.4.2 dependencies.
pending.defined-unary-operator-highest: PENDING positive-control source shape .neg. x * y where .neg. is a valid defined unary operator returning an encoded derived or integer-like value. The oracle distinguishes (.neg. x) * y from .neg.(x*y) without observing call order.
pending.defined-binary-operator-lowest: PENDING positive-control source shape x .op. y + z with a valid defined binary operator whose result encodes the already interpreted right operand. The oracle is an independent literal result and not the number or order of function invocations.
pending.dotted-name-not-intrinsic-symbol-precede: PENDING positive-control source shape comparing a dotted operator such as .starstar. with an extended intrinsic ** on the same operand family. The oracle must distinguish lowest defined-binary precedence from exponentiation precedence and cite 10.1.2.9 for dotted spelling.

requirements.title: The general expression form establishes same-class operand grouping for interpretation
requirements.definition: Within a syntactic class, the general expression form in 10.1.2 establishes the order in which operands are combined for interpreting the expression, unless parentheses change that order. This is an interpretation rule; it does not require any particular runtime evaluation order for operand computations.

review_rationale: Independent source review in doc/source_audits/batch_100.json reads all27 original base units and81 fine units of 10.1.3,10.1.4 and10.1.5.1 in full, together with the cited 7.x,10.1.6 through10.1.12 and15.4.3.4.x material and the registered 10.1.2 grammar catalogues, and independently enumerates the evaluation freedoms in scope before comparing them with the candidate. This scope is where the processor latitude lives, so a permission wrongly promoted to a requirement, or a plan that infers behaviour from evaluation order, would corrupt every later expression fixture. The review confirms that the IF, WHERE and FORALL side-effect permission and the permission for pure elemental operations to be performed in any order or simultaneously are both dispositioned as permissions rather than requirements; that the conditional skipped-evaluation effect carries no side-effect oracle; and that the freedoms owned by 10.1.7,10.1.8 and10.1.6.3 are recorded as oracle boundaries and dependencies rather than as locally owned requirements. Table10.2 is substantively correct, with the enumeration-type and character-kind distinctions preserved. No plan infers anything from which operand was evaluated or in what order, asserts a result that a mathematically equivalent rewrite could change, or relies on a floating-point tolerance, and grouping of an associative intrinsic operation is not claimed to be value-observable. The expression grammar remains owned by the registered 10.1.2 catalogues and intrinsic assignment by 10.2.1.3. All facets remain pending source plans; no case, execution, oracle or fixture approval is created.
